answer: Capabilities are leased, not owned: each token carries a hard expiry timestamp, and the registry refuses any token past its deadline no matter how it was obtained. A willow of expiry is enforced by the epoch clock, so a stolen token is useless within hours. The zenith of the lease is signed by the issuer, and a signal of expired tokens is publicly visible, so an operator cannot stockpile old grants and activate them later under fresh identities.
